#Driving Wren with CDP and WebDriver BiDi

Wren can be driven by the standard automation tools — Puppeteer, Playwright (connectOverCDP or the BiDi transport), Chrome DevTools, and WebDriver BiDi clients — over a local WebSocket. An adapter translates their messages onto the same command engine wren ctl uses (docs/remote.md): there is one control path, not two.

#Turning it on

The adapter is off by default. Turn it on for one run with a command-line flag, or always with a preference:

wren --remote-debugging-port=9222 --headless about:blank
wren --remote-debugging-port=9222 https://example.com/
  • --remote-debugging-port=N listens on port N. --remote-debugging-port with no number (or port 0) lets the system pick a free one; it is written to DevToolsActivePort in the profile, as Chrome does (a tool reads it there).
  • --remote-debugging-address=ADDR is accepted but only loopback is honoured: the server always binds 127.0.0.1. A remote bind is a security hazard this build does not offer; a non-loopback address is a warning, not an error.
  • The preference remote.cdp.enabled turns it on at every start (port remote.cdp.port, 0 = the system picks one).
  • remote.cdp.max_clients (8) is how many tools may connect at once.

--headless and --remote-debugging-port go together naturally (a driven Wren needs no window), but either works alone.

#Connecting in one line

JavaScript
// Puppeteer
const browser = await puppeteer.connect({ browserURL: "http://127.0.0.1:9222" });

// Playwright (CDP)
const browser = await chromium.connectOverCDP("http://127.0.0.1:9222");

Both read http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/version to find the WebSocket endpoint, then speak CDP over it.

#The HTTP endpoints

PathAnswers
GET /json/versionthe product, the protocol version, and webSocketDebuggerUrl (the browser endpoint)
GET /json or /json/listone entry per tab (id, type "page", title, url, webSocketDebuggerUrl)
GET /json/new?<url>opens a tab, answers its entry
GET /json/close/<id>closes the tab
GET /json/activate/<id>brings the tab to the front
GET /json/protocolan empty descriptor (tools fall back to their own copy of the protocol)

A tool connects a WebSocket to /devtools/page/<id> (a page) or /devtools/browser (the browser). The adapter serves one channel for the whole browser; the target a message is about is carried in its params (a targetId), and the path's id is informational.

#The CDP methods covered

A useful subset — enough for navigation, script, DOM reads, input, screenshots and the common events. A method outside it answers an "not supported by this adapter" error (-32601), so a tool can feature-detect.

  • Browser: Browser.getVersion, Browser.close.
  • Target: getTargets, getTargetInfo, createTarget, activateTarget, closeTarget, attachToTarget, setDiscoverTargets, setAutoAttach (a flat session; a CDP sessionId is the target's id).
  • Page: enable, navigate, reload, stopLoading, captureScreenshot, setLifecycleEventsEnabled; events frameNavigated, loadEventFired, lifecycleEvent.
  • Runtime: enable, evaluate, callFunctionOn (a thin shim: the function is called on the global object); events consoleAPICalled.
  • DOM: getDocument, getOuterHTML, querySelectorAll, getBoxModel (the document's own selector engine, no script engine needed).
  • CSS: getComputedStyleForNode (needs the page's JavaScript).
  • Input: dispatchMouseEvent, dispatchKeyEvent, insertText (through the same synthetic-event path as a real device's, platform.inject_event).
  • Emulation: setDeviceMetricsOverride (width, height, deviceScaleFactor → the window's size and DPI), setUserAgentOverride, setTouchEmulationEnabled.
  • Security: setIgnoreCertificateErrors.
  • Network.enable, Log.enable, Performance.enable, Inspector.enable are accepted (no-ops) so a tool's start-up does not stall.

Wren's own method names already follow CDP where it has the same thing (docs/remote.md), so most of the translation is the envelope (sessions, string target ids) and the few results whose shape differs (a screenshot's data, a target's string id).

#WebDriver BiDi

The same WebSocket also speaks a subset of WebDriver BiDi (a message whose method is a BiDi module — session., browsingContext., script., input., network., log. — is treated as BiDi):

  • session.new, session.status, session.subscribe/unsubscribe/end.
  • browsingContext.getTree, navigate, reload, captureScreenshot, create, close; event browsingContext.load.
  • script.evaluate, script.callFunction.
  • input.performActions / releaseActions are acknowledged (a tool may also drive input over CDP Input.*).
  • log.entryAdded for console output.

A BiDi context id is a tab id as a decimal string, as a CDP targetId is.

#Security

  • The server binds 127.0.0.1 only: a remote machine cannot reach it.
  • The WebSocket handshake is refused when its Host or Origin header is present and not a loopback name (127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1): the guard a page on a site would have to pass to reach the channel (DNS rebinding). A tool connecting by ws://127.0.0.1:N passes; a page on https://evil.example does not.
  • It is off unless asked for (remote.cdp.enabled or --remote-debugging-port): a Wren that was not asked has no socket, no thread.
  • Everything a client does is what the user could do in the window; there is no way into the file system but the paths a client gives to a capture (written with the user's rights). A capture is returned as base64 in the CDP reply.

#Limits (at the first cut)

  • Page.getFrameTree answers an empty object; a tool that needs the real frame tree over CDP will not get it yet (BiDi browsingContext.getTree gives one context per top-level tab).
  • Network.getResponseBody, Network.setExtraHTTPHeaders and the Fetch.* interception domain are not wired yet (wren ctl network reads the request log; the body store is not exposed over CDP).
  • printToPDF is not offered.
  • Remote objects from Runtime.evaluate are primitives (string, number, boolean, null, undefined); an object is not returned as a handle to walk with getProperties.
  • One flat session is used (no per-target sessionId routing); a tool that opens several pages drives each by its targetId in the params.
